doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

title: Closing thanks, equipment and building a base on tour
summary: Wrap-up, carrying equipment and arranging rentals while building an audience.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I have to say it’s been a very inspiring conversation.
Yeah well thank you very much.
So logistically we have to get you, you’ve got, I wonder if you have a roadie coming in for all this stuff.
That’s a luxury that none of us can afford.

Not this — well you know you have to build a career and a base and everything. So coming up here, this was really my first time, me and the group coming through this area and everything. But next time I come a lot of this stuff could be rented by venues. Like we’re going to New Mexico in a week or so and of course they know we can’t bring this stuff so they’re making arrangements to have all this stuff there for us and rented and everything. But right now, sometimes you have to get in the door first, and then when you get in the door you can say okay listen, we came here, we brought all this equipment up and everything, now if you want us back you’re going to have to make arrangements to either go by the local college — most colleges, you go by them you know and then talk to the band director and everything. He’ll let you use their equipment for the evening, especially if you give a donation to the school for a minimal thing.
